title: Imputation without works follows because blessedness needs remission (Psalm 32)
source_text: XXXVIII. Unde est quod Apostolus in sequentibus probat Deum imputare homini justitiam sine operibus, quia nemo pervenit ad vitam & beatitudinem, & ex consequenti justus apud Deum habetur, nisi cui Deus peccata remittit; juxta illud Davidis, Beati quorum remissae sunt iniquitates, & quorum tecta sunt peccata. Nam ut multa bona opera reperiri possint in eo qui opus habet remissione peccatorum, si tamen Deus illum pro justo habet, necessario imputat illi justitiam sine operibus illis quae lex gratiae opposita exigit ad hoc ut hominem justum pronunciet. Siquidem opera illa constant omnibus numeris absoluta legis observatione, qua destitutus est ille qui vel semel legem transgressus est, quique ulla peccati remissione opus habet.
pass_a_gloss: Hence in what follows the Apostle proves that God imputes righteousness to a person without works, because no one arrives at life and blessedness—and consequently is held just before God—except the one to whom God remits sins; according to David's word: Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. For although many good works may be found in the one who needs remission of sins, if nevertheless God holds him as just, he necessarily imputes righteousness to him without those works which the law opposed to grace requires in order to pronounce a person just. Since those works consist in observation of the law complete in every respect, of which the one who has even once transgressed the law—and who needs any remission of sin—is destitute.
pass_b_english: Psalm 32: blessedness requires remission—so imputation is without law-perfect works.
Anyone needing forgiveness already lacks the flawless obedience law demands.

lemmas.gloss: Blessed are those whose [iniquities] are remitted
